core_obligations: Reduce the three properties to finite purely inseparable base changes, using the purely inseparable characterization of each of geometric regularity, geometric normality and geometric reducedness (proof lines 4626-4630).
Note that the base change of a smooth morphism is smooth, so it suffices to prove that a scheme smooth over a field is regular, normal and reduced (proof lines 4631-4634).
Finish: a scheme smooth over a field is regular by the specialization of the smooth-implies-regular principle to a field base, and a regular scheme is normal (proof lines 4635-4639).
proof_roadmap: Common reduction to purely inseparable base changes (proof lines 4626-4630).
difficulty_reason: For a smooth morphism X to Spec(k) with k a field, the lemma concludes that X is geometrically regular, geometrically normal and geometrically reduced over k (statement lines 4616-4621). The proof reduces the three properties simultaneously to a statement about a single smooth scheme over a field: by the purely inseparable characterizations already available it suffices to show that the base change along any finite purely inseparable extension is regular, normal and reduced, and the base change of a smooth morphism is smooth (proof lines 4626-4634). There it is enough to prove the three properties for a scheme smooth over a field, which the author does in two steps: smoothness over a field implies regularity by the specialized lemma, and a regular scheme is normal by the standard criterion (proof lines 4635-4639). The claim is H2: the reduction is a shared one for three properties, with two cited inputs finishing the job.
